relevance_reason: This is a case report of a Japanese patient with CLPED1 who has a novel homozygous PVRL1 nonsense mutation.

findings.statement: Yoshida et al. (2015) reported a 7-year-old Japanese boy with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome. He was the first child of a consanguineous marriage. He had hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia, along with a distinctive facial appearance with cleft lip/palate, cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers, and mild mental retardation. Scanning electron microscopy of the hair showed pili torti and pili trianguli et canaliculi.
quotes: A 7-year-old Japanese boy, the first child of a consanguineous marriage, showed hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia, the unique facial appearance with cleft lip/palate, cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers and mild mental retardation.
Scanning electron microscopic examination of the hair demonstrated pili torti and pili trianguli et canaliculi.

findings.statement: Yoshida et al. (2015) analyzed exon 2 of the PVRL1 gene in the Japanese boy with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome and found a novel homozygous nonsense mutation, c.400C>T (p.Arg134*). Both of his consanguineous parents were heterozygous for the mutation. The authors noted that all 4 PVRL1 mutations reported in this syndrome so far, including this one, produce truncated proteins that lack the transmembrane and intracellular domains of nectin-1. These domains are needed to start the cell-cell adhesion process.
quotes: Mutation analysis of exon 2 of PVRL1 revealed a novel homozygous nonsense mutation, c.400C>T (p.Arg134*). His parents were heterozygous for the mutant alleles.

All four PVRL1 mutations identified in cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome to date, including this study, resulted in truncated proteins that lack the transmembrane domain and intracellular domain of nectin-1

The paper links heterozygosity for the PVRL1 W185X mutation, which causes CLPED1 when homozygous, to sporadic non-syndromic CL/P (OFC7), a phenotype this entry includes.

findings.statement: Sözen et al. (2001) found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation W185X and sporadic, non-syndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (CL/P) in northern Venezuela. Homozygosity for the same mutation causes the autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome CLPED1 on Margarita Island.
quotes: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X, results in an autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome on Margarita Island, CLPED1 (ref. 1).

phenotypes.text: non-syndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate

relevance_reason: Positional cloning identified PVRL1 as the gene for autosomal recessive CLPED1.

findings.statement: By positional cloning, Suzuki et al. (2000) identified PVRL1, which encodes nectin-1, an immunoglobulin-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule of the NAP cell adhesion system, as the gene responsible for autosomal recessive cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4).
quotes: Here we describe positional cloning of the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2), which we identify as PVRL1, encoding nectin-1, an immunoglobulin (Ig)-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule that is part of the NAP cell adhesion system.

phenotypes.text: cleft lip with or without cleft palate

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (2000) noted a high frequency of CLPED1 on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea and suggested that it might result from resistance of heterozygotes to infection by alpha-herpesviruses, since nectin-1 is the principal cell surface receptor for these viruses (HveC).
quotes: Nectin-1 is also the principal cell surface receptor for alpha-herpesviruses (HveC; ref. 7), and the high frequency of CLPED1 on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea might result from resistance of heterozygotes to infection by these viruses.

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (2000) designated the autosomal recessive cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome CLPED1, previously known as ED4.
quotes: (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2)

relevance_reason: Maps the Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia (ED4), i.e. cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome, to 11q23 through linkage disequilibrium mapping.

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (1998) described Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia (ED4) as an autosomal recessive disorder. Its features are unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate.
quotes: Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia (ED4) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate.

findings.statement: Suzuki et al. (1998) used an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy for linkage disequilibrium mapping and placed the ED4 gene at 11q23. Haplotype analysis of 4 complex Margarita Island ED4 families narrowed the gene to an interval of about 1 to 2 Mb, spanned by just 2 YACs.
quotes: We have used an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy to carry out linkage disequilibrium mapping of the ED4 gene to 11q23.
Haplotype analysis of four complex Margarita Island ED4 families localized the ED4 gene to an approximately 1-2-Mb interval spanned by just two YACs.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It names the combination of syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia and cleft lip/palate, which matches the features of the cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome. No patient, inheritance or variant details are available.

findings.statement: Zlotogora (1994) reported on the association of syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip/palate.
quotes: Syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip/palate.

relevance_reason: Reports two sibs with cleft lip/palate, sparse hair/pili torti, malformed ears, syndactyly and mental retardation, consistent with the CLPED1 phenotype, with suggested autosomal recessive inheritance.

findings.statement: Zlotogora et al. (1987) reported 2 sibs with a syndrome of cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair, malformed protruding ears, and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes. The older child also had mental retardation and pili torti.
quotes: Two sibs with a syndrome including cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair, malformed protruding ears, and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes are reported.
The older child also has mental retardation and pili torti.

findings.statement: Zlotogora et al. (1987) concluded that the syndrome in 2 affected sibs was most probably inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder.
quotes: This syndrome is most probably inherited as an autosomal recessive disorder.

relevance_reason: The title shows the paper describes syndactyly occurring with ectodermal dysplasia and cleft lip and palate, which is the phenotype in this entry. Only the title was available, so no patient, family, or variant details could be taken from it.

findings.statement: Zlotogora and Ogur (1988) reported syndactyly together with ectodermal dysplasia and cleft lip and palate.
quotes: Syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, and cleft lip and palate.

relevance_reason: The paper describes two sibs from a consanguineous family who had cleft lip and palate, ectodermal dysplasia and syndactyly. This combination is the CLPED1 phenotype.

findings.statement: Oğur and Yüksel (1988) reported 2 Turkish brothers, born to parents who were second cousins, with tetramelic syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip and palate, renal anomalies, and mental retardation.
quotes: Two Turkish sibs, products of a second cousin marriage, with tetramelic syndactyly, ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip and palate, renal anomalies, and mental retardation are reported.

findings.statement: Oğur and Yüksel (1988) reported 2 affected brothers born to second-cousin parents. They compared these sibs with previously reported cases and discussed the mode of transmission.
quotes: Two Turkish sibs, products of a second cousin marriage
Similarities between these two brothers and previously reported cases and their mode of transmission are discussed.

relevance_reason: Case report of 3 sibs with Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome (ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly), born to consanguineous parents, supporting autosomal recessive inheritance of CLPED1.

findings.statement: Rodini and Richieri-Costa (1990) reported 3 Brazilian brothers, born to normal consanguineous parents (F = 1/16), who had ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly of fingers 2-3, accessory nipples, and ear anomalies. The authors discussed the similarities of these brothers to previously reported cases of Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome.
quotes: We report on 3 Brazilian brothers born to normal consanguineous parents (F = 1/16) and presenting ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly of fingers 2-3, accessory nipples, and ear anomalies.

findings.statement: The occurrence of the disorder in 3 brothers born to normal consanguineous parents (F = 1/16) was considered by Rodini and Richieri-Costa (1990) in discussing an autosomal recessive pattern of inheritance for Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome.
quotes: Autosomal recessive ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, and syndactyly: the Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome.
The similarities of these 3 brothers to previously reported cases and the pattern of inheritance are discussed.

relevance_reason: The paper is the original clinical description of an autosomal recessive ectodermal dysplasia syndrome seen in inbred families on Margarita Island, Venezuela. This is the population and syndrome that the CLPED1 entry covers.

findings.statement: Bustos et al. (1991) described 27 individuals from 7 families who were probably related to each other. All had ectodermal dysplasia along with other anomalies. Females were affected as severely as males, and expressivity varied. The families came from a relatively isolated, inbred population on Margarita Island (Nueva Esparta State) in northeastern Venezuela. The authors concluded that the clinical picture did not fit any known ectodermal dysplasia.
quotes: We describe 27 individuals of 7 families related to each other with high probability who showed manifestations of ectodermal dysplasia and other anomalies affecting females as severely as males with variable expressivity.

These families were detected in a relatively isolated and inbred population with very small neighbouring communities from a Caribbean Sea island, Margarita Island, in Northeastern Venezuela (Nueva Esparta State).

findings.statement: Bustos et al. (1991) found that all parents of affected individuals were normal and that both sexes were equally affected in an inbred population. They concluded that the condition was a newly recognized autosomal recessive dysplasia/malformation syndrome.
quotes: All parents were normal.
We believe that this condition constitutes a newly recognized autosomal recessive dysplasia/malformation syndrome of ectodermal dysplasia.
